purpose: Complete Lane B Figure 3 by testing whether determinant order is preserved along variance-equivalent k_eff contours in the nonlinear Chapter 2 model.

correlation_construction.reason: If each copy uses a common trajectory with probability q and otherwise an independent trajectory from the same marginal distribution, pairwise copy correlation is q^2=rho for any scalar copy-level statistic.
correlation_construction.expected_distinct_trajectory_support: k*(1-sqrt(rho)) + 1 - (1-sqrt(rho))^k for rho>0; k for rho=0
correlation_construction.k_equals_1_rule: rho is undefined/irrelevant for one copy, so all k=1 rows reuse the independent baseline.

grid.primary_display: median S/C/I across the six pre-existing seeds
grid.seed_robustness: store determinant-order counts across all six seeds

decision_rule: k_eff is not a sufficient statistic if at least one exact k_eff contour contains more than one median determinant order under the same nonlinear response operator.
claim_boundary: This is a post-hoc structural/figure-completion analysis motivated by the already observed nonlinear reduction failure; it is not a preregistered confirmatory test.
rho is exact pairwise copy correlation in this clone-mixture construction, not an empirical field synchrony estimate.
Whole-trajectory clone mixing is paired with the separately frozen identity-preserving shared-event correlation robustness audit; neither implementation alone carries the general claim.
A contour that preserves order does not rescue k_eff as sufficient; sufficiency requires preservation across all states with the same k_eff.
I/C is a diagnostic of reduction failure, not a universal rho-invariant law.
